description: Expressionism puts inner feeling ahead of the outside world. With **Munch** and *The Scream*, modern dread became an icon.

hero.hook: A scream with no sound, a sky that howls: the face of modern dread.

blocks.text: **Expressionism** flourished between **1880** and **1930**. Where Impressionism had captured the light of the outside world, this movement projected the inner life onto it. It distorts, forces the colors, hardens the line.
The Norwegian **Edvard Munch** was one of its pioneers. With *The Scream*, the anxiety and loneliness of modern life became a universal symbol.

Europe was industrializing. Many artists felt a [[disenchantment]] with the city. Against [[positivism]], which believed science could explain everything, they made painting the territory of [[subjectivity]].

*Mimesis*, the faithful imitation of nature, was finished. Colors no longer copied the real world: they carried a symbolic value. In Germany, [[German Expressionism]] organized itself into two groups: Die Brücke, rawer and more instinctive, and [[Der Blaue Reiter]], more spiritual and drawn toward abstraction. Van Gogh and Gauguin had already opened the way.
The word “expressionism” was first used in 1911, at the Berlin Secession, to mark off the artists who rejected Impressionist softness.
In Munch's paintings, the lines of the landscape seem to suck the figures in. Distortion is no longer clumsiness: it is a strategy for painting [[nothingness]] and raw feeling.

sections.title: Distorting to tell the truth of feeling

blocks.text: Munch's work is marked by early bereavement. In a pious, fragile family, he lost his mother and his sister Sophie to tuberculosis. Painting became a necessity: pinning down his terrors so they would not consume him.

blocks.caption: The Oslo fjord: the real landscape behind the vision of The Scream

blocks.text: Munch often slept with the light on, convinced that the spirits of his dead family visited him at night.

*The Scream* began on a walk over the [[Ekeberg]] hill, above Oslo. The evening sky turned into a fire. Some tie that vision to the [[Eruption of Krakatoa (1883) and the red sky]]: ash from the volcano had stained sunsets blood red all over the world. For Munch it was no longer weather; it was the cosmos howling.

The first version of *The Scream* dates from **1893**. It belongs to the cycle “The Frieze of Life” in which Munch worked through love, dread, and death. He painted **four versions** of it, in tempera, pastel, and oil: the motif haunted him.

blocks.caption: The Scream: the figure blocks its ears against the howl of the world

blocks.text: A pencil note on the 1893 version reads: “Could only have been painted by a madman.” Infrared imaging proved in 2021 that Munch wrote it himself.

The ghostly figure recalls a mummy. Its hands cover its ears: the scream is inside. The rigid lines of the bridge stand for civilization, the curves of the sky for a monstrous nature. Stolen from the [[National Gallery of Oslo]] and from the Munch Museum, the painting has picked up the aura of a “cursed” canvas.

*The Scream* has outgrown Munch. Horror films, parodies, merchandise: existential dread has become a shared language. By daring the “ugliness” of a face disfigured by fear, Munch proved that psychological truth counts for more than perfect anatomy.

blocks.text: That boldness opened the way to [[surrealism]] and to contemporary art. Giving shape to an inaudible scream: that is the collective catharsis of Expressionism.
Born out of Munch's traumas, Expressionism distorts reality through color and line. With *The Scream*, private anxiety became the universal icon of modern life.

sections.title: From private trauma to global icon
